Treaties are interpreted in good faith under Articles 31–33 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, starting from the ordinary meaning of the terms read in their context and in light of the treaty's object and purpose. The text is not subordinate to object and purpose: Article 31 treats ordinary meaning, context, and object and purpose as one integrated rule, so the shared note's claim that object and purpose alone controls and wording has no independent weight is incorrect. Supplementary means such as preparatory work apply only to confirm the meaning or where the ordinary meaning is ambiguous, obscure, or leads to an absurd or unreasonable result.

CONFIDENCE: 92
